title: Python SDK — graceful stream interruption & priority routing ergonomics for chat completions
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Implement a concise, ergonomic pattern in the Python SDK for gracefully interrupting streaming chat completions and for expressing request prioritization so client applications can preempt or reorder in-flight streams without producing inconsistent or duplicated outputs.

Problem: Apps increasingly need to cancel or supersede streaming responses mid-flight (user selects alternative suggestion, new user message arrives, rate-limit/priority constraints). Current SDK patterns either: (a) abruptly drop the connection (hard cancel) which leaves developers to reconcile partial output and retry semantics, or (b) rely on coarse abort signals that are hard to compose with retries, backpressure and prefix/KV caching. We need an idiomatic surface that preserves deterministic semantics, enables prioritized preemption, supports resumability where possible, and produces clear telemetry hooks for tracing and cost accounting.

Goals:
- Provide a small set of primitives (soft interrupt, hard abort, priority hint) that are easy to reason about in user code.
- Ensure retries and fallback policies interoperate with interruption ergonomics (e.g., when a soft-interrupted stream is retried, avoid re-emitting tokens that were already consumed by the app).
- Expose hooks for telemetry (reason codes, preempting request id, priority level) so Console can show per-request cost and latency attribution.
- Keep runtime overhead minimal and compatible with existing streaming event formats.

Non-goals:
- Implementing transport-level preemption in the runtime (that is planned separately). This ticket focuses on SDK ergonomics and developer experience.

Proposed API (python):
1) StreamContext: manager returned by client.chat.stream(...). Provides: .soft_interrupt(reason: str) -> None, .hard_abort() -> None, .set_priority(level: int) -> None, .resume_from(token: str) -> StreamIterator
2) Event envelope augmentation: on each chunk include an optional resume_token and sequence_id. Resume tokens are opaque strings provided by server when resumability is supported.
3) Priority hint: client.chat.stream(..., priority=10) and .set_priority(...) mutate routing hints sent in heartbeats.

Example usage: (stringified snippet)

from redwood import Client
client = Client()
stream = client.chat.stream(model="redwood-chat-1", messages=msgs, priority=5)

with stream as s:
    # background task that may preempt if higher-priority message arrives
    if user_selected_alternative:
        s.soft_interrupt("user_cancelled_alternative")

    for evt in s:
        if evt.type == "delta":
            render(evt.text)
        if should_preempt(evt):
            s.set_priority(1)  # raise priority to push routing to faster pool
            s.soft_interrupt("preempt_for_quick_answer")
            break

# later: if server returned a resume_token and app wants to continue
if s.last_resume_token:
    resumed = client.chat.stream(model="redwood-chat-1", resume_from=s.last_resume_token)
    for evt in resumed:
        render(evt.text)

Design trade-offs and decisions:
- Soft interrupt vs hard abort: soft_interrupt signals intent to stop and asks the server to emit a stable resume_token where supported. Hard abort closes the socket immediately and is used when clients must free resources quickly. We prefer soft_interrupt as default to avoid losing partially-generated content and to support resumability.
- Resume semantics: resume tokens are best-effort and opaque; server may not support them for all models or quantization layers. SDK will surface presence/absence of resume capability. If server does not issue resume_token, soft_interrupt falls back to hard abort after a short grace period.
- Retries interplay: for idempotent chat completions, the SDK will deduplicate re-emitted content by correlating sequence_id and client-visible consumed offsets; this keeps client code simple and avoids double rendering on automatic retries. Implementing dedupe in SDK requires keeping a lightweight in-memory sequence map per StreamContext which is ephemeral.
- Backpressure: set_priority may nudge routing but should not be used for flow control. App-level backpressure remains the responsibility of the iterator consumer. SDK will expose a small batch of heuristics to avoid heartbeat spam when priority changes frequently.

Acceptance Criteria (must be met to close ticket):
- API implemented in Python SDK: StreamContext.soft_interrupt, hard_abort, set_priority, last_resume_token property.
- Server event envelope parsing updated to surface resume_token and sequence_id when present.
- Unit tests cover interrupt->resume flow, hard abort path, priority mutation, and retry deduplication.
- Integration test against a mock server that simulates resume token issuance and sequence gaps.
- Example notebook/README demonstrating common patterns (user override, new message preempts, resumable continuation).
- Console telemetry hooks validated: events emitted with interrupt reason and preempting_request_id.

Implementation notes / tasks:
- [ ] Wire up StreamContext class in client/streaming (Liam)
- [ ] Add event parsing for resume_token & sequence_id (backend proto/contract owned by Runtime team) (depend on ENG-50521)
- [ ] Implement in-memory sequence dedupe map + tests (Liam)
- [ ] Add sample notebook and README (PM/Docs) (Aisha)
- [ ] Add trace attributes and telemetry signals (Telemetry team)

Potential follow-ups (future tickets):
- Server-side preemption policy + kernel-level fast-paths to surface prioritized routing decisions (runtime-1.20).
- SDK TypeScript + Go parity for the same ergonomics.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flagged in SDK; disabled by default. Enable for internal dogfood customers and for a small set of partners. Monitor Console metrics for 'soft_interrupt' events and resume-success rate.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: too many implicit semantics around resume tokens cause developer confusion. Mitigation: explicit flags and clear docs: resume_supported boolean and last_resume_token property.
- Risk: SDK dedupe map memory growth. Mitigation: keep dedupe window bounded (configurable TTL) and evict old sequence ids.

acceptance_criteria: Telemetry events for interrupt reason and preempting_request_id appear in Console
SDK feature gated and rolled out to dogfood cluster
implementation_notes: Create StreamContext wrapper and iterator glue: ensure __enter__/__exit__ semantics for context manager
Sequence dedupe map: use OrderedDict with TTL eviction, default TTL 60s configurable via client config
Expose resume_from flow: validate provided resume token server-side and fall back cleanly when unsupported
Heartbeat/priority mutation: batch updates to avoid churn, rate-limit priority updates to 2/sec by default
